fullPassage: Email is one of the most widely used forms of communication today. Did you know that the seemingly innocent act of looking through emails or checking your inbox has an environmental impact? In reality, email travels through an energy-consuming network, contributing to climate change on our planet. Storing countless email messages in data centers creates carbon emissions. These data centers rely on huge servers to store and access data at all times. Because the centers use electricity to run the servers and to cool down the large amounts of heat that they generate, they consume a significant amount of fossil fuels. Mike Berners-Lee, the British researcher and author of How Bad Are Bananas?: The Carbon Footprint of Everything, looked at our average email traffic. For example, a short phone-to-phone email has a carbon footprint of 0.2g of CO₂ emissions. But, a long email, which takes about ten minutes to write and three minutes to read on a computer, has a footprint of 17g of CO₂ emissions. So, something as simple as deleting unnecessary email messages can help to save the Earth.
title: Green Your Inbox
